extracted.intended_audience: community members and environmental justice advocates submitting public comments on environmental rules, permits, and enforcement (especially in Georgia)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and submitting effective public comments on environmental rulemakings, permits, enforcement decisions, and local legislation; includes what to research, what to include, what to avoid, and post-submission actions. Geared to community members and advocates who want their input to influence agency decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, detail, and direct applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments must be "clearly written, detailed, and directly applied" to the proposed regulation or permit under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep comments clear, organized, fact-driven, and to the point. Make sure every point you raise is tied to the specific proposal or permitting decision so the agency can act on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the correct comment type/venue
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the issue is a Rulemaking, Permitting, Enforcement Decision, or Lawmaking comment and use the appropriate portal or process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access federal proposals at regulations.gov for rulemakings; use Georgia's EPD website or GEOS portal for permits; submit comments on consent orders for enforcement decisions; participate in local government meetings for local legislation. Selecting the correct category ensures the comment is docketed and reaches the right decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct thorough research and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct thorough research before the comment period begins; collect relevant data, community observations, and documentation; review public files and access government records; identify local impacts (schools, parks, sensitive populations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather scientific data, monitoring results, photos, and public records. Identifying nearby sensitive receptors (schools, parks, elderly housing) helps demonstrate concrete impacts. Start research early to meet deadlines and strengthen claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear, organized, and concise in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep comments "clear, organized, fact-driven, and to the point."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure comments logically (intro, facts/evidence, legal issues, requested action). Avoid long emotional rants; agencies respond more readily to well-organized submissions. Use headings or numbered points where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish credentials and personal/community connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish your credentials and personal connection to the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain who you are (resident, parent, local organization) and why you are affected. Personal standing and concrete connections to harms increase the persuasive weight of a comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all concerns and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Include ALL concerns (future legal challenges depend on this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise every substantive issue you want preserved on the administrative record so they cannot later be waived. Do not omit arguments you may want to pursue legally later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific sources and provide credible facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific citations with sources; include relevant scientific data or credible facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with citations to studies, government data, monitoring results, or public records. Specific citations make it easier for agencies to verify and act on your points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell your community's story with concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell your community's story with concrete examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific incidents, dates, photos, or observations to illustrate harms. Concrete examples humanize impacts and clarify the real-world effects of agency decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State explicit requested actions
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicitly what action you want the agency to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about remedies or changes (e.g., deny permit, require monitoring, strengthen limits). Clear requested outcomes help agencies and the public understand the purpose of the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include essential contact and docket information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your name, address, email, and phone number; agency name, regulation name, and docket ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing full contact and docket information ensures your comment is associated with the correct record and that the agency can contact you if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specific legal violations and ask for agency responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify specific violations of law you've found and include questions requiring agency response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out statutes, regulations, or permit conditions that are not being met and request the agency explain or remedy them. Posing clear questions can compel a formal agency reply on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsubstantiated, irrelevant, or improper content
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't include theories without evidence, gossip, vague concerns, personal financial information, hearsay, or attacks on specific officials. Avoid making unsubstantiated claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stick to verifiable facts and avoid ad hominem attacks or irrelevant personal data. Unsubstantiated or inappropriate material can undermine credibility and may be redacted or ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and follow up after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission: Track your comment via regulations.gov using your tracking number, attend public meetings, engage local officials, and consider press outreach to maintain momentum on your issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tracking to confirm docketing, show up at hearings, contact elected officials, and use media to keep attention on the issue. Post-submission engagement increases the chance of agency or political response.
